themes_detail.label: Street Deterioration Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints in CD 302 surged to 63 reports THIS WEEK, a 191% spike above the 8-week average of 21.6 complaints per week (z-score: 4.73), suggesting accelerating pavement, pothole, or sidewalk failure across Fort Greene and Brooklyn Heights.
evidence: 63 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 21.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.73 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Long-standing CB budget request for 'Other transportation infrastructure requests' suggests chronic underinvestment in street maintenance
reporting_angles: Walk neighborhood streets to document potholes, cracked sidewalks, and dangerous conditions; interview residents and elderly pedestrians about safety hazards
Contact DOT to determine if weather events, deferred maintenance, or construction projects are driving the spike; check permit filings for clues

themes_detail.label: Real-Time Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Real Time Enforcement complaints jumped to 8 reports THIS WEEK, a 611% spike from the 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 4.26), suggesting a sudden increase in parking, traffic, or vendor enforcement activity—or resident pushback against new enforcement operations.
evidence: 8 Real Time Enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average
Z-score of 4.26 indicates significant statistical anomaly
Illegal parking remains top complaint category (6,306 over 90 days), suggesting enforcement crackdown could be reactive
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD and DOT to learn if new enforcement initiative or detail was deployed to CD 302 this week; ask for complaint data
Interview residents on both sides: those who support crackdown on parking violations vs. those experiencing aggressive ticketing

themes_detail.label: Street Sign Structural Failures
themes_detail.summary: Dangling street sign complaints spiked to 5 reports LAST WEEK, a 344% increase above the 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 4.96), indicating potential public safety hazard from deteriorating street furniture across the district.
evidence: 5 dangling street sign complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.96 indicates high statistical significance
Coincides with broader street condition spike (63 complaints THIS WEEK), suggesting systemic infrastructure neglect
reporting_angles: Photograph dangling or damaged street signs in Fort Greene and Brooklyn Heights; document locations and safety risks (pedestrians, vehicles)
Contact NYC DOT about inspection schedules and maintenance backlogs; determine if budget constraints or deferred maintenance are responsible

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints jumped to 4 reports LAST WEEK, a 700% spike from the 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.95), suggesting a sudden outbreak of graffiti, bill posting, or unauthorized signage—possibly tied to upcoming 395 Flatbush redevelopment or campaign activity.
evidence: 4 illegal posting complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average
Z-score of 4.95 indicates statistically significant anomaly
395 Flatbush Avenue Ext. Redevelopment in active public review phase—may be correlated with development signage or protest postings
reporting_angles: Canvas Fort Greene and Brooklyn Heights for recent illegal postings; photograph and document types (political, commercial, graffiti) to identify source
Cross-reference timing with 395 Flatbush ULURP review schedule and recent community board meetings to see if posting is development-related

themes_detail.label: Sewer Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints spiked to 19 reports 3 WEEKS AGO, a 322% increase above the 4.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.7), suggesting possible pipe failures, backups, or overflow issues that may still be unresolved.
evidence: 19 sewer complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 4.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.7 indicates high statistical significance
Chronic CB budget request for 'Other expense budget request for DEP' suggests persistent infrastructure underinvestment
reporting_angles: Contact DEP to determine if sewer failures were reported and repaired; ask about pipe age, maintenance schedules, and wet weather overflow events
Interview residents in areas with sewer complaints about sewage backups, odors, or street flooding; document conditions with photos
